input.subject: Boiler losing pressure – 18 Orchard Court (ref R/1)
input.body:
Dear Mrs Haddad,

Thank you for reporting the boiler losing pressure and cold radiators (ref R/1). We're treating this as urgent.

Our records show you as the tenant of Flat 4, 18 Orchard Court, but your first email asked us to send someone to Flat 6. So that we send the engineer to the right boiler, please could you confirm:
1. Is it the heating in Flat 4 that isn't working, and does the boiler in the shared utility cupboard on your landing serve Flat 4 (rather than Flat 6)?
2. Is anyone in your household elderly, unwell, very young or otherwise vulnerable to the cold?

We've noted that you can be at home on Thursday afternoon. We will confirm an appointment once an engineer is arranged – nothing is booked yet.

In the meantime, please:
- Don't open the boiler casing or attempt any repairs yourself.
- If you notice water leaking from the boiler or pipes, turn the boiler off and place a towel or bowl underneath.
- If you ever smell gas, leave the property, don't use switches, and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.
- Use a portable electric heater if you have one to keep warm.

We'll follow up with you by tomorrow morning at the latest.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance Team

data.reasoning:
The classifier flags this as an emergency, and even without confirmed vulnerability, no heating in late September cold weather warrants urgency. But there's a real blocker: it's unclear which boiler or flat is affected, and there's no contractor on record, so I can't dispatch anyone yet. I should message the tenant to clarify the flat in question, confirm whether Flat 6 was an error, and ask about any vulnerable occupants.

Given the conflicting flat details, possible communal responsibility, and missing contractor/landlord contacts, I'll record the facts, place a short hold, and escalate to a human rather than guess. Since landlord identity depends on which flat is actually affected, I'll hold off on notifying any landlord to avoid contacting the wrong one, and leave that step for the human to handle once confirmed.
